newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bonds weaken in spots, supply mounts.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bonds weaken in spots, supply mounts.

text.p: U.S. corporate high-grade bond spreads widened in spots on Wednesday as new issues hit the market at a brisk pace, while high-yielders were weaker but for fresh paper, dealers said.

Topping the new issue slate, Abbey National Plc issued $500 million AA3/A-plus rated perpetual subordinated reset notes via a Salomon Brothers syndicate. The notes are non-callable for 10 years and were priced as 7.35s to yield 78 basis points over the 10-year U.S. Treasury note.
The issue was increased in size by $200 million to meet strong investor demand, a Salomon source said.

Campbell Soup Co also stepped in with $300 million AA3/AA-minus rated 10-year notes through lead manager Goldman Sachs & Co. The notes were priced as 6.90s to yield 6.945 percent or 35 basis points over the Treasury curve. The notes have a make-whole call at Treasuries plus five basis points.

Consolidated Natural Gas Co set $150 million A1/AA-minus rated 30-year senior debentures with a 10-year put option through lead manager Chase Securities Inc. The debt was priced as 6.875s to yield 6.752 percent or 16 basis points over the 10-year T-note.

Investment grade trading desks reported no "real" erosion in spread into the close, although they noted some were slightly wider in the wake of brisk new issuance. They stressed the market was still cash rich, however.

Reflecting the marginal move, Citicorp's 7.25 percent bonds were seen bid at 78 basis points over U.S. Treasuries compared with Tuesday's 77 basis point spread. The notes were priced via Bear Stearns & Co.
Prices also suffered in sympathy with U.S. Treasuries, which fell from highs when the government said real earnings rose 0.8 percent in September, traders said.

Treasuries managed slight gains in early trade after the Commerce Department said its consumer price index rose by 0.3 percent in both overall and core categories. The 30-year Treasury bond closed down 7/32 to yield 6.86 percent.
Turning to high-yield trade, prices were scattered lower as investors focused on what promises to be a busier new issue slate through October and November.

But the pattern of bidding for new debt continued with Aames Financial Corp's issue of $150 million senior notes due 2003, priced through Bear Stearns & Co. The notes, priced at 99.714 for a spread of 275 basis points over Treasuries, traded up to 100-5/8, 101-7/8 market, a trader said.
The notes are rated Ba3 by Moody's Investors Service.

Losers in secondary trade included Trump Castle notes based on new litigation against Donald Trump, one trader said. Separately, Adelphia Communications debt faded to 102-1/4, 102-3/4 market, down more than one point on the day.
Harrah's Jazz notes fell 1/2 point to 57 bid after gaining one point in Tuesday's trade.
